name: Mumbai Eastern Freeway

timeline.event: First phase, from P D'Mello Road to Panjarpol, opens to traffic
Full 16.8 km freeway up to Ghatkopar becomes operational

history: The Eastern Freeway lets drivers move between south Mumbai and the eastern suburbs without a single traffic light. Built by the MMRDA, it runs mostly on long elevated viaducts past the old dock lands and even passes through twin tunnels cut into a hill near Panjarpol. It opened in stages in 2013 and 2014. Unusually for a big Mumbai road project, it is completely toll-free.
facts: 16.8 km long with no traffic signals and no toll.
Includes twin road tunnels near the Anik–Panjarpol hills.
Much of the route is one of the longest elevated road stretches in Mumbai.
Connects to the Eastern Express Highway at Chheda Nagar, Ghatkopar.

sources.title: MMRDA — Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority
